title: Is there an improved RTP for MV/MZ?

posts.author: shIxx
posts.body:
Hello Community,
I'm wondering if there is an improved version of the RTP where the tiles are arranged at the correct height, like in this
blog post
. I've been searching the internet for hours but can't find anything.
With GIMP I can swap out some tiles, but rearranging them, etc. is too complicated for me.
This is such an important improvement that I think someone must have done it already.
If anyone has a link I would be very grateful.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
shIxx said:
rearranging them, etc. is too complicated for me.
Click to expand...
Why? If you can replace tiles, then why can't you drag the pasted image up a few pixels? Which parts of the tutorial are too complicated?
shIxx said:
This is such an important improvement that I think someone must have done it already.
Click to expand...
Not that I've ever seen - because it's very basic to do in an image editor, everyone I've seen just does it themselves.
Also, the objects take up more space on the sheet this way, so a person couldn't just make a replacement of the original tilesets with all of the objects shifted up - they won't all fit on the sheet at the same time. So people choose which items they want to use on a given map and edit those onto a sheet.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
shIxx said:
It looks like I need to practice setting up grids, integrating templates, etc. and then follow the tutorial.
It will definitely take many hours.
Click to expand...
Why?
It takes maybe ten seconds to click into Image Settings and define your grid as 48x48 (and if you're going to be using RPG Maker a lot, you can even save that as your default grid size and only take the ten seconds once).
What does "integrating templates" mean and why would you have to do it? There's nothing like that in the tutorial, and I've certainly never done anything like that to copy tiles between sheets.
You open the two images, select the tile(s) containing the original object, copy, select tiles on the other tab, paste, drag it up 24 pixels. That's the entire tutorial
I have no idea what you think would take hours about the process.

posts.author: bgillisp
posts.body: I do it with a 48 x 24 grid, and snap to grid in GIMP. Then it lines up better. But same idea as Turan said otherwise.
